HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P) NOTE

History:
• Chief complaint: Pain/burning on urination for 6 days.  
• Course: Gradual onset, persistent; “hurts when I pee,” malodorous urine.  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent mid-lower abdominal/suprapubic pain (7/10, comes and goes); small “spots” of blood in urine.  
• Denies: Fever, flank/loin/back pain, nausea/vomiting, vaginal discharge, urinary retention. Able to eat and drink normally.  
• Previous episodes: None.  
• Triggers/precipitants: Denies recent dehydration, excessive exercise, or increased sexual activity.  
• Gynecologic: Regular periods. No abnormal vaginal discharge.  

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).  
• No prior kidney disease, urinary infections, surgeries, or other chronic illnesses reported.  

Allergies:
• Clindamycin (reaction not specified).

Medications:
• Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily.  
• Antibiotic for current infection prescribed today (name/dose/route/frequency not documented—pending pharmacy pick-up).  

Social / Family History:
• Lives with friends; works as a support worker.  
• Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine per week.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Family history: No significant illnesses reported.  

Physical Examination:
(tele-consultation; no in-person exam)  
• General: Appears well on video, conversant.  
• Vital signs: Not recorded.  
• Abdominal / flank / pelvic exam: Not performed.  
• Mental status: Alert and oriented.  
• Other systems: Not recorded.

Impression:
Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis (urinary tract infection) – most consistent with 6-day dysuria, foul-smelling urine, suprapubic pain, and mild hematuria, without systemic or flank features.

DDx considerations consistent with transcript:  
1. Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis – as above (highest likelihood).  
2. Urethritis (STI-related) – possible but less likely; no discharge or high-risk sexual history elicited.  
3. Distal urinary tract calculi – low likelihood; hematuria present but no colicky/radiating or flank pain.

Management Plan:
• Pharmacologic: 3-day course of oral antibiotics for cystitis (prescription sent electronically to patient’s chosen pharmacy; specific drug details not documented).  
• Supportive care:  
  – Increase fluid intake to 2.5–3 L water daily.  
  – Optional cranberry juice.  
  – Over-the-counter urinary alkalinizing sachets (details to be provided in notes).  
• Monitoring/Safety-net advice:  
  – Obtain a home thermometer; check temperature regularly.  
  – Seek medical review if pain worsens, develops flank or back pain, fever, difficulty passing urine, or if symptoms do not improve or recur.  
• Follow-up: No routine review required if symptoms resolve; contact service promptly if above red-flag symptoms occur or if recurrence noted.  
• Pharmacy: Medication expected to be ready at Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy within ~1 hour; patient plans to collect at lunchtime.

Patient Summary:
35-year-old woman with 6-day history of dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, and mild hematuria, classical for acute uncomplicated cystitis. No systemic or upper-tract features. Empiric 3-day antibiotics prescribed with hydration and safety-net advice.

Key Takeaways:
• Start antibiotics as soon as collected and complete full 3-day course.  
• Drink 2.5–3 L of water daily; consider cranberry juice and urine-alkalizing sachets.  
• Re-contact a clinician immediately if fever, flank pain, worsening symptoms, or recurrence occurs.

Next Steps:
• Patient to pick up antibiotic prescription today.  
• Obtain home thermometer for self-monitoring.  
• If no improvement in 48–72 h or recurrent episodes develop, arrange urine dip/culture and further evaluation.
